steps.message:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Odufor, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 20.32 | 0.13606 | 0.13606
2 | 851.16 | 1.1039 | 1.2399
3 | 2511.9 | 15.803 | 17.043
4 | 1345 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as A-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Odufor, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note – Station Odufor, Etche LGA**

The interpreted layer model shows four layers with resistivities increasing from a shallow, relatively conductive topsoil (20.32 Ω·m, 0.136 m thick) to a more resistive second layer (851.16 Ω·m) and a highly resistive third layer (2511.9 Ω·m, extending to ~17 m depth), before decreasing to 1345 Ω·m in the underlying basal layer.

Applying the standard curve-type convention: resistivities for layers 1-2-3 (20.32 < 851.16 < 2511.9) give an **A** segment, while layers 2-3-4 (851.16 < 2511.9 > 1345) give a **K** segment. The correct curve type is therefore **AK**, not a pure A-type as stated in the file. The resistivity drop in the fourth layer is inconsistent with a single-letter A classification, which requires continuously increasing resistivity throughout.

Recommend updating the station record to reflect the AK curve type.

{"curve_type_stated": "AK", "label_issue_flagged": true}
